questions.stem: A 29-year-old Mrs. Bishnoi has regular, infrequent menstrual cycles occurring at an interval of 35-36 days. What is the usual timing of ovulation in this lady?
questions.solutionHtml:
14 days before menstruation

Ovulation occurs 14 days before menses, regardless of cycle length.




Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No: 392

questions.stem: Which of the following is the dominant hormone in the luteal phase?
questions.solutionHtml:
Progesterone

Progesterone is the dominant hormone during the luteal phase.




Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No: 392

questions.stem: Which of the following hormones is responsible for the maintenance of endometrial thickness in the post-ovulatory phase?
questions.solutionHtml:
Progesterone

Progesterone is mainly responsible for the maintenance of endometrial thickness in the post-ovulatory phase.




Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No: 392-393

questions.stem: Positive feedback action of estrogen for inducing luteinizing hormone surge is associated with which of the following steroid hormone ratio in peripheral circulation?
questions.solutionHtml:
High estrogen: low progesterone

The feedback action of estrogen for inducing luteinizing hormone (LH) surge is associated with high estrogen: low progesterone.




Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no: 392-393

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains the mechanism behind an increase in LH secretion just before ovulation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Positive feedback by estrogen

Increased luteinizing hormone (LH) secretion just before ovulation is due to positive feedback by estrogen.




Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no: 392-393, Human Physiology: An Integrated Approach (5th Edition) Page No 849, Costanzo's Physiology 6th Edition, Page No: 473-474.

questions.stem: Corpus luteum of pregnancy is maintained by:
questions.solutionHtml:
HCG

Human chorionic gonadotropin (HG) causes the persistence of the corpus luteum and prevents menstruation in pregnancy.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition, Page No: 1042
